correctness.rationale: At each x except the finitely many base tent breakpoints, the unsorted tents have first-order velocities -b_i' on the rising halves, d_i' on the falling halves, and zero elsewhere. Finiteness keeps distinct base-height blocks disjoint for sufficiently small |h| at that x. Inside a tied block, each baseline coordinate is the same, so the sum of p-th powers of the increments agrees exactly with the unsorted sum regardless of the ordering at h. The order-statistic sup-norm bound and the common compact support give an integrable dominator; integrating yields exactly the two half-lifetime factors for all finite p>=1, including p=1. On a compact C^1 track the same bounds give Lipschitz continuity and the metric length theorem gives the stated integral. For the example [g,4),[-g,6), the top layer is x+|g| for small |g| at each fixed x in (0,2); on any compact subinterval the resulting one-sided quotients already exclude a strong L2 derivative. Independently, for 0<h<1 the shorter perturbed tent is nested in the longer, and direct integration over the moving birth and apex strips gives ||lambda(h)-lambda(0)||_p^p = h^p[5-h(3/2-3/(p+1))], consistent with speed sqrt(5) for p=2.
residual_risks: The proof assumes a fixed finite number of positive-length bars tracked by differentiable endpoints at the point; zero lifetimes, births or deaths of bars, infinite bars, truncated layers, and p=infinity are not covered.
The supplied checker tests exact rational secants with a tolerance at the smallest step only; it is not the basis of the theorem.

Independence from overlaps at all finite p is useful for interpreting the result; the positive-length tie example marks a concrete difference between speed and strong differentiation.
